observations: The three cited s-stems are instrumentally related. The selected masculine heads qualify a warrior, thief and fish.
Bāla qualifies the activities as battle, risky theft and motion owing to water. Prakriyāsarvasva also names a water-bearing cloud.
The six outputs accompany tat and intransitive vṛt. The special explicitly stated relation is a manner qualifier.
The compound commentaries identify ī for the chosen two water compounds and oppose the geographic anu+ap under ū.
Nyāsa 4.4.28 expressly uses the inner ac compound result as the recipient of its ṭhak rule, with prati/anu loman operands. The independently closed 5.4.75 inner cases receive zero repeat credit.
Bāla reports Śabdenduśekhara's general prathamā analysis of adverbials beside the explicit accusative support taught here.
Kāśikā's ca expressly supplies paripārśva beside parimukha.
Nyāsa gives avoidance and all-round service, with separate avyayībhāva and prādi construction. Tattva reports the pair again and refers to both meanings for paripārśva.
The addressed page has sāhasikaṃ naram. The commentary's vigraha explicitly says sahas is force and the person acts by it.
The next rule of royal conduct addresses sāhasikān sarvabhūtabhayāvahān with masculine accusative plural agreement.
Benfey lists a sāhasa+ika parse, and Hema's independent 6.4.28–29 labels name ikaṇ on the paired manner and pari words.
decisions: Use tena at 4.4.27 for three exact instrumental lexemes. At 4.4.28 use tat with manner ACC. The two relations retain distinct input grades and the same outer ṭhak owner.
Project 6.3.97/98 and 2.1.12 are matched by exact wording to other local labels 6.3.96/97 and 2.1.11. No numerical alias changes a source.
Select ī in lexical pratīpa/anvīpa; real geographic anūpa remains a separate positive output outside the selected manner request.
Inner samāsānta ac and its loman ṭi deletion precede outer ṭhak. An avaloma cannot enter 4.4.28 solely through the wider inner license.
Retain the same case forms under the two source-qualified parimukha analyses. Accept one paripārśva extension from ca without assigning a new arbitrary base by similarity.

The 8.344 force address admits the direct sahas path on the authority of Medhātithi. 8.347 independently anchors plural saṃdhi and agreement. Benfey's sāhasa parse has positive lexical-source status; its specific affix history remains Open.
The cloud report has its own denotation. The reported prathamā case is a competing general analysis with its exact interplay with tat Open. Neither changes these selected masculine case keys.
Do not transfer ikaṇ or an unlabelled lexicon ika into the Pāṇinian ṭhak history. Corresponding whole words may agree while the marker effects remain owner-specific.
